transcript.text: Thank you all for joining me. As you know, the district is considering a classroom pilot of an adaptive writing platform for the coming fall term. The vendor has offered it at no cost, and the platform can provide individualized writing prompts and feedback. Before I approve the proposal, I need your operational findings. The draft doesn't yet specify the participating grade, data settings, teacher support, or family orientation arrangements, so I'd like each of you to weigh in on what you're seeing from your respective areas. Let's start with the instructional coach — what are you finding regarding classroom readiness and teacher support needs?

transcript.text: I should share what I've observed. I actually saw this platform in action in two seventh-grade classrooms, and a key finding was that the useful feedback from the platform depended on a six-week cycle with one coached teacher-planning session each week. I recorded this in my coaching notes, but I realize those notes haven't been attached to the draft proposal.

Two key data privacy terms: student accounts must operate in local-only mode, and identifiable writing data may be retained for exactly 30 days. These specifics aren't reflected in the draft proposal yet, and they have direct implications for the data settings Dr. Shah asked about.

commitments.detail: Weekly coached teacher-planning sessions will be scheduled throughout the six-week pilot cycle to ensure the platform's feedback is effective.
Student accounts will operate in local-only mode, and identifiable writing data retention will be capped at 30 days per the vendor's final agreement.
Family orientation materials and a live session will be provided in English, Spanish, and Somali before the pilot launches.

The draft proposal will be updated to specify seventh grade as the participating grade, local-only data mode, 30-day retention limit, six-week duration with weekly coached planning sessions, and trilingual family orientation in English, Spanish, and Somali.
